assets.label: Sled-drone pisteur — identité, deux orientations
assets.prompt:
Generate an ORIGINAL new design proposal for the 2D Yautja fan-game La Longue Chasse, based on a requested name with only partial or no precise visual specification. This is NOT a canonical film replica. Exactly TWO complete SIDE profiles SIDE BY SIDE: left view facing RIGHT, right view facing LEFT, independently draw the same construction/anatomy in opposite orientations and identical scale. Entire silhouettes must fit in the central 80 percent of each half with generous blank outer and central margins. Pure uniform MAGENTA #FF00FF background. Detailed hand-painted bitmap, no ground shadow, scenery, text, watermarks, diagram labels or grid. No human, Yautja rider, passengers, cargo, trophies, UI or effects. Empty vehicle chassis: removable weapons and props excluded. Small UNMANNED tracking drone sled PROPOSAL for first pursuit tier, entirely mechanical low oval armored body, forward compact multi-lens sensor cluster, short antenna mast, pair of compact protected antigravity pods, rear battery casing. NO saddle, cockpit, hands or occupant. Sensor lamps unlit glass with tiny amber status dot, no scanning beam.
Production correction: use a strict flat orthographic side-view camera with zero three-quarter perspective. Exactly two independently authored opposing side profiles in one horizontal row. Preserve a wide empty magenta gutter and at least 10 percent blank margin around each complete silhouette. Every requested removable module must stay absent, closed, folded, stowed, or represented only by an empty hardpoint exactly as specified.

references.role: Recovered user request normalized as an explicit original design proposal

notes: OpenAI ImageGen identity candidate. Static review sheet only; no gameplay or animation acceptance implied.
Clean unmanned opposing side profiles: sensor cluster, antenna, two compact antigravity pods and rear battery are readable; no saddle, cockpit, hands, occupant or scanning beam.
Source and public copies remain byte-identical; color-key transparency is applied by the production review renderer.
